[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"IO Operations in Pandas (CSV, Parquet, JSON, SQL)"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Efficient data ingestion and export are foundational skills for any data scientist or engineer. Pandas provides a robust suite of Input/Output (IO) tools designed to read and write data across a multitude of formats seamlessly."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. CSV Operations"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Comma-Separated Values (CSV) are the most common file format for tabular data. Pandas utilizes read_csv() to parse files into DataFrames and to_csv() to export them."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"import pandas as pd

# Reading a CSV file
df = pd.read_csv('data.csv', usecols=['id', 'name', 'value'], chunksize=10000)

# Writing to a CSV file without index
df.to_csv('output.csv', index=False)"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Parquet Operations"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"Apache Parquet is a columnar storage format optimized for performance and compression, making it ideal for big data workflows. It retains pandas data types better than CSV."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"# Writing a DataFrame to Parquet
df.to_parquet('data.parquet', engine='pyarrow', compression='snappy')

# Reading a Parquet file
df_parquet = pd.read_parquet('data.parquet', columns=['id', 'value'])"},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"3. JSON Operations"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) is standard for web APIs. Pandas handles various JSON structures using the orient parameter (e.g., 'records', 'split', 'index')."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"# Reading JSON records
df_json = pd.read_json('data.json', orient='records')

# Exporting to JSON
df.to_json('output.json', orient='records', indent=4)"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"4. SQL Database Operations"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"Pandas integrates directly with SQL databases using SQLAlchemy engines, allowing you to read query results directly into DataFrames and write DataFrames back into tables."},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"from sqlalchemy import create_engine

# Create a database engine
engine = create_engine('sqlite:///mydatabase.db')

# Reading from a SQL query
df_sql = pd.read_sql('SELECT * FROM users WHERE active = 1', con=engine)

# Writing a DataFrame to a SQL table
df.to_sql('users_backup', con=engine, if_exists='replace', index=False)"},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices"},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use chunksize in read_csv() when handling massive files that exceed available RAM."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Prefer Parquet over CSV for intermediate storage to preserve data types and reduce file sizes."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Always close or properly manage SQLAlchemy connections when executing heavy database operations."}]
